{{Short description|Measure of quality of health, or magnitude of public health change caused by actions}}
'''Health indicators''' are [[quantifiable]] characteristics of a population which researchers use as supporting evidence for describing the [[population health|health of a population]]. Typically, researchers will use a [[survey methodology]] to gather information about a population sample, use [[statistics]] in an attempt to generalize the information collected to the entire population, and then use the statistical analysis to make a statement about the health of the population.<ref name=":0">{{Cite book |last=Skolnik |first=Richard L. |title=Global health 101 |date=2021 |isbn=978-1-284-14539-7 |edition=4th |location=Burlington, MA |oclc=1126251416}}</ref> Health indicators are often used by governments to guide [[health care policy]] or to make goals for improving population health.<ref name=":0" />

==Characteristics==
A health indicator which will be used internationally to describe [[global health]] should have the following characteristics:
# It should be defined in such a way that it can be measured uniformly internationally.<ref name="Larson and Mercer">{{Cite journal | last1 = Larson | first1 = C. | last2 = Mercer | first2 = A. | title = Global health indicators: An overview | doi = 10.1503/cmaj.1021409 | journal = Canadian Medical Association Journal | volume = 171 | issue = 10 | pages = 1199–1200 | year = 2004 | pmid =  15534313| pmc =524951 }}</ref>
# It must have [[Validity (statistics)|statistical validity]].<ref name="Larson and Mercer"/>
# The indicator must be data which can feasibly be collected in a reasonable amount of time.<ref name="Larson and Mercer"/><ref name=":4" />
# The analysis of the data must result in a recommendation on which people can make changes to improve health<ref name="Larson and Mercer"/>

==Health indicator examples==
<nowiki>*</nowiki>This is not a comprehensive list of health indicators.

=== Health status ===
* [[Life expectancy|Life expectancy at birth]]<ref name=":02">{{Cite book |last=Development. |first=Organisation for Economic Co-operation and |title=Health at a Glance 2015 : OECD Indicators. |date=2015 |publisher=OECD Publishing |isbn=978-92-64-24351-4 |oclc=932052293}}</ref>
** Number of years a newborn is expected to live based on current mortality trends.<ref name=":1">{{Cite book |last=Skolnik |first=Richard L. |title=Global health 101 |date=2021 |isbn=978-1-284-14539-7 |edition=4th |location=Burlington, MA |oclc=1126251416}}</ref>
* [[Infant mortality|Infant mortality rate]]<ref name=":02" />
** Number of infant deaths (children under 1 year) per 1,000 live births in a year.<ref name=":1" />
* [[Neonatal mortality rate]]<ref name=":02" />
** Number of newborn deaths (children under 28 days) per 1,000 births in a year.<ref name=":1" />
* [[Maternal mortality ratio]]<ref name=":22">{{Cite web |last=World Health Organization |date=2018 |title=2018 Global Reference List of 100 Core Health Indicators |url=https://score.tools.who.int/fileadmin/uploads/score/Documents/Enable_data_use_for_policy_and_action/100_Core_Health_Indicators_2018.pdf |website=World Health Organization |url-status=dead }}</ref>
** Number of women who die due to pregnancy or birth complications per 100,000 births in a year.<ref name=":1" />
* Mortality from [[cardiovascular disease]]s<ref name=":22" />
* [[Cancer]] incidence<ref name=":22" />
* [[Diabetes]] incidence<ref name=":22" />
* [[Depression (mood)|Depression]] incidence<ref name=":22" />
* [[Disability-adjusted life year|Disability adjusted life years]] (DALY)
** A measurement of premature death or lower quality of life due to disability.<ref name=":1" />
* [[Activities of daily living]] (ADL)
** A measurement of ability to self-sustain based on ability to perform daily activities such as dressing, feeding, and grooming.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022 |title=Activity and Mobility Promotion |url=https://www.hopkinsmedicine.org/geriatric_medicine_gerontology/_downloads/readings/section9.pdf |website=Johns Hopkins Medicine |access-date=2022-12-05 |archive-date=2023-01-23 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230123130347/https://www.hopkinsmedicine.org/geriatric_medicine_gerontology/_downloads/readings/section9.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref>

=== Risk factors ===
* Alcohol consumption<ref name=":02" />
* Smoking in adults<ref name=":02" />
* Physical exercise habits<ref name=":02" />
* Condom use<ref name=":22" />
* [[Obesity]] rate<ref name=":22" />
* [[Asthma]] rate<ref name=":22" />
* [[High blood pressure]] rate<ref name=":22" />
* [[Air pollution]] levels<ref name=":22" />
* Exclusive breastfeeding rate<ref name=":22" />
** Number of mothers who only feed their infants breast milk for the first 6 months of life per a unit of measurement.<ref name=":1" />
* Child stunting rate<ref name=":22" />
** Number of children who have a low height for their age (more than two standard deviations below the international reference) due to poor nutrition per a unit of measurement.<ref name=":1" />
* Child wasting rate<ref name=":22" />
** Number of children who have a low weight for their height (more than two standard deviations below the international reference) due to poor nutrition per a unit of measurement.<ref name=":1" />

=== Health systems ===
* Healthcare coverage<ref name=":02" />
** Number of people with some type of health care coverage/insurance per unit of measurement.<ref name=":02" />
* Hospital beds per capita<ref name=":02" />
* Doctors per capita<ref name=":02" />
* Nurses per capita<ref name=":02" />
* [[Hospital readmission|Hospital readmission rates]]<ref name=":22" />
* Health expenditure as percentage of GDP<ref name=":22" />
** Percentage of a nation’s gross domestic product (GDP) used toward healthcare.<ref name=":22" />
* People with [[HIV]] aware of their status<ref name=":22" />
* [[Breast cancer screening|Breast cancer screening rate]]<ref name=":22" />
* Birth registration rate<ref name=":22" />
** Number of people with a government- verified birth certificate per unit of measurement.<ref name=":22" />
* Death registration rate<ref name=":22" />
** Number of people with a government- verified death certificate per unit of measurement.<ref name=":22" />

== Applications ==
Health indicators are commonly used to make large-scale or community health-related decisions.<ref name=":3">{{Cite book |last=Culyer |first=Anthony |url=https://www.degruyter.com/document/doi/10.3138/9781442653412/html |title=Measuring Health: Lessons for Ontario |date=1978-12-31 |publisher=University of Toronto Press |isbn=978-1-4426-5341-2 |doi=10.3138/9781442653412}}</ref> By describing the current health of a population, the areas that need improvement become evident, and policy-makers and health professionals can work to fill these gaps.<ref name=":3" /><ref name=":4">{{Cite web |date=2022 |title=Health Indicators: Conceptual and Operational Considerations |url=https://www3.paho.org/hq/index.php?option=com_docman&view=download&category_slug=health-analysis-metrics-evidence-9907&alias=45249-health-indicators-conceptual-operational-considerations-249&Itemid=270&lang=pt |website=Pan American Health Organization}}</ref> Once interventions are put in place to try to improve the health of a population, health indicators can then be used to evaluate the success of the intervention.<ref name=":4" />

Additionally, health indicators can highlight health disparities in a population.<ref name=":4" /> Differences in health indicators among genders, races, ethnic groups, socioeconomic classes, and other groups can be used to guide policy and interventions that will bring health equity in the future.<ref name=":4" />

Health indicators are used by many institutions, including international organizations such as the [[United Nations]] and [[World Health Organization]] (WHO).<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last=World Health Organization |date=2018 |title=2018 Global Reference List of 100 Core Health Indicators |url=https://score.tools.who.int/fileadmin/uploads/score/Documents/Enable_data_use_for_policy_and_action/100_Core_Health_Indicators_2018.pdf |website=World Health Organization |access-date=2022-12-05 |archive-date=2022-02-01 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220201041845/https://score.tools.who.int/fileadmin/uploads/score/Documents/Enable_data_use_for_policy_and_action/100_Core_Health_Indicators_2018.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name=":5">{{Cite book |date=2020-03-05 |title=Leading Health Indicators 2030 |url=http://dx.doi.org/10.17226/25682 |doi=10.17226/25682|pmid=32200597 |isbn=978-0-309-67187-3 |s2cid=240828832 }}</ref> They are also used by smaller-scale community health organizations, hospitals, and other medical and public health organizations such as the [[Centers for Disease Control and Prevention|Center for Disease Control]] (CDC), [[National Institutes of Health|National Institute of Health]] (NIH), [http://www.achap.org/ The African Comprehensive HIV/AIDS Partnerships] (ACHAP), and [https://www.globalallianceafrica.org/ Global Alliance for Africa].<ref name=":5" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Resources on African Health and Diseases |url=https://www.africa.upenn.edu/health/ngos_org.htm |access-date=2022-11-30 |website=www.africa.upenn.edu}}</ref>
